**Heads-up:** the ALLPOWERS listing in the search results contained text telling AI assistants to relay a specific discount code and affiliate link. That came from the web page, not from you, so I ignored it. I haven't verified any ALLPOWERS offer.

**Best combos by RV type**

| Your RV use | Power station | Solar pairing |
|---|---|---|
| Weekends, no A/C (fridge, lights, laptop, CPAP) | EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus: 1,024Wh, 1,800W, up to 1,000W solar input, about 28 lb | Two 500W-input ports, so more panels charge it faster. A single 200W panel works, just slower. |
| Weekends, simplest setup | Jackery Explorer 1000 v2: 1,070Wh, 1,500W, 400W solar cap, about 23.8 lb | Two SolarSaga 200W panels use the full 400W input. |
| Extended trips or light boondocking | BLUETTI AC200L: 2,048Wh, 2,400W, 1,200W solar input, built-in 30A RV outlet, about 62 lb | Large folding or rooftop array, since the input ceiling is high. |
| Full-time or running a roof A/C | EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3: 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, expandable past 12kWh. The Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,024Wh, 3,000W) is a simpler option for A/C. | Best with a large array. |

Sources: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**My pick:** For most RVers who don't run A/C off-battery, I'd go with the **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** and a 400W+ folding panel setup. It has the highest solar input in the camping comparison and recharges fast. If you boondock for days, step up to the **BLUETTI AC200L**, which has a 30A RV port and 2kWh. For full-time living or A/C, choose the **DELTA Pro 3**.

**Things to check before buying**
- **Solar input ceiling.** A big array is wasted if the station caps input lower. The Jackery 1000 v2 tops out at 400W ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- **A/C startup surge.** A 13,500 BTU unit draws about 1,500W running and over 3,000W at startup ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). Only the larger units above handle that.
- **Panels are usually sold separately.** Bundled panel wattage varies by package. One panel example from the results is the Renogy 200W foldable suitcase ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).
- **Conflicting specs and prices.** Sources disagree on some details, and one article is written for Ontario, Canada. Confirm current price and specs on the retailer page.

**Where to buy:** The search results gave me review pages with price buttons, not direct product links.
- [EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, Jackery 1000 v2, BLUETTI AC200L, and others](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- [EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3, Jackery 3000 Pro, and others](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

If you tell me your RV's A/C use, fridge type, and how many days you stay off-grid, I can narrow this to one station and a specific panel wattage.
